brands.name: Gash Surfboards
brands.location_label: Fingal Head, New South Wales, Australia
brands.short_description: Australian custom surfboards from Greg Brown — Torquay-born Gash templates now built out of Fingal Head, from twins and keels to step-ups.

models.name: Custom Shorty
models.description: Board Featured: This board is at five ten, rounded square with a bone tint and custom GASH x Soar Red glass on fins. Planshape: Narrower nose with plenty of outline curve, slight hips coming into the tail brings width in under your backfoot. The tailpad is not particularly wide. Fins: Thruster. Can be a Quad, but NOT 5 fins. Tail: Squash, Swallow, Rounded Pin. Size: Five Seven to Six Four. Colour: Available tints in DeWALT yellow, Institution Orange, Butthole Purple, GASH red, Black, Bone.

models.name: Custom Twin
models.description: Board Featured: Five Six, Soar x GASH black glass ons with a DeWALT yellow lapped resin tint. Planshape: Not bulbous in front 1/3 like typical twin. More even nose entry with outline running a little paralleled into rear 1/3. Rolled deck for thickness through stringer, allowing slightly dropped rails with more sensitivity. Fins: Twin only. Placement, tow & camber can vary to suit individual & wave range. Tail: Swallow. Tips narrowed to allow pivot from backfoot.

models.name: Custom Step-Up
models.description: Board featured: Six Nine, bone tint, custom GASH x Soar red glass on fins. Planshape: Narrow nose, curvacious through middle and slightly straighter into rear third. Refined tail like a blade for extra bite. Thickness pushes forward of centre for extra paddle power but fine nose tip. Fins: Thruster only. Tail: Swallow, Rounded Pin, Semi Pin, Narrow Wing, Mellow SC and Flat at tip. Size: Six three to Six nine.

models.name: Custom Twin Keel
models.description: Board Featured: Six Ten, Soar x GASH black glass on Keels with a Butthole Purple lapped resin tint. Planshape: Mid length Keel, deep swallow. Fins: Black Soar Bolt ons, available with futures. Tail: Swallow. Tips narrowed to allow pivot from backfoot. Rarely a rounded pin.
